record.paper_title: Open problems in dynamics and related fields
record.context_brief: Nondegenerate matrix-valued maps and VWA avoidance
record.original_question: Can one find reasonable and checkable conditions for a smooth map f:U⊂R^k→M_{m×n}(R) that generalize nondegeneracy of vector-valued maps and imply that almost every point of f(U) is not very well approximable?

evidence.quote: QUESTION 35 (D. Kleinbock, G. Margulis (see [144], Sec. 6.2)) . Find reasonable and checkable conditions for a smooth map f : U (⊂ Rk ) → Mm× n(R) which gener-alizes nondegeneracy of vector-valued maps and implies tha t almost every point of f(U ) is not VWA.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$ denote the space of real $m\times n$ matrices. A matrix $Y\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$ is called very well approximable (VWA) if there exists $\varepsilon>0$ such that the system of inequalities
$$\|Y\mathbf{q}+\mathbf{p}\|^{m} \le \|\mathbf{q}\|^{-n-\varepsilon}$$
has infinitely many solutions $(\mathbf{p},\mathbf{q})\in\mathbb{Z}^{m}\times(\mathbb{Z}^{n}\setminus\{0\})$, where $\|\cdot\|$ denotes a fixed norm. (Equivalently, $Y$ has Diophantine exponent strictly greater than $n/m$.) For $n=1$ this recovers the usual notion of a VWA vector in $\mathbb{R}^{m}$.

For a smooth (e.g. $C^{\infty}$) map of vectors $f:U\to\mathbb{R}^{N}$ defined on a connected open set $U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{k}$, one says that $f$ is nondegenerate at $x_{0}\in U$ if there exists $\ell\in\mathbb{N}$ such that the partial derivatives of $f$ at $x_{0}$ of order at most $\ell$ span $\mathbb{R}^{N}$, and $f$ is nondegenerate if it is nondegenerate at almost every $x_{0}\in U$. A classical theorem asserts that whenever $f:U\to\mathbb{R}^{N}$ is nondegenerate, almost every point of $f(U)$ (with respect to Lebesgue measure pushed forward from $U$) fails to be VWA.

Problem. Formulate reasonable and verifiable conditions on a smooth map
$$f:U\subset\mathbb{R}^{k}\longrightarrow M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$$
that generalize the notion of nondegeneracy of vector-valued maps and that imply the following conclusion: for Lebesgue-almost every $x\in U$, the matrix $f(x)\in M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$ is not very well approximable. In particular, identify checkable geometric/algebraic conditions on $f$ (or on its image submanifold of $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$) under which the pushforward of Lebesgue measure on $U$ by $f$ is an extremal measure on $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$.
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made. Aka, Breuillard, Rosenzweig, and de Saxcé (GAFA 2018, "Diophantine approximation on matrices and Lie groups") formulate a criterion for extremality of analytic submanifolds of $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$ in terms of algebraic (representation-theoretic) obstructions, showing that the almost-sure Diophantine exponent of an analytic submanifold depends only on its Zariski closure, and giving an effective computation in the rational case. Further work (e.g. Beresnevich–Kleinbock on quantitative non-divergence, and recent papers on systems of small linear forms and twisted approximation on manifolds) provides additional sufficient conditions. However, a fully general clean "nondegeneracy" condition encompassing all known cases for arbitrary smooth maps into $M_{m\times n}(\mathbb{R})$ does not yet appear settled in full generality, so the problem is best described as partially solved.

status_evidence.title: Diophantine approximation on matrices and Lie groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the general problem of extremality for metric Diophantine approximation on submanifolds of matrices, formulating a criterion for extremality in terms of algebraic obstructions.
status_evidence.claim: A criterion generalizing nondegeneracy to matrix submanifolds, implying extremality, has been formulated and proved for analytic submanifolds.

status_evidence.title: On metric diophantine approximation in matrices and Lie groups
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the diophantine exponent of analytic submanifolds of the space of m by n real matrices, answering questions of Beresnevich, Kleinbock and Margulis.
status_evidence.claim: Earlier announcement explicitly addressing questions of Kleinbock and Margulis about extremality on matrix submanifolds.

status_evidence.title: Quantitative non-divergence and Diophantine approximation on manifolds
status_evidence.snippet: Beresnevich–Kleinbock work on quantitative non-divergence on manifolds, extending tools toward matrix settings.
status_evidence.claim: Further partial progress via quantitative non-divergence techniques.
